58531-history-of-the-second-massachusett.title: Official Reports, Diaries And Rosters
58531-history-of-the-second-massachusett.creator: Caroline E. Whitcomb
58531-history-of-the-second-massachusett.description: A book by Caroline E. Whitcomb. Few batteries during the Civil War saw more actual service than that known officially as the 2d Massachusetts Light Artillery, but more generally called Nims' Battery. Its career is well worth recording and the part it played in the campaigns of the Department of the Mississippi and the Gulf was by no means inconsiderable in the history of the war.

If the repute of the writer or the attraction of the rhymes commanded interest, these might be copied, reach an expanding circle, and achieve celebrity. In such manner, partly through the agency of Michelangelo himself, the sonnets of Vittoria Colonna came into circulation, and obtained an acceptance ending in a printed edition.

arxiv-2105-12983.title: Correlation Filter of 2D Laser Scans For Indoor Environment
arxiv-2105-12983.creator: Kirill Krinkin, Anton Filatov
arxiv-2105-12983.description: Abstract Modern laser SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) and structure from motion algorithms face the problem of processing redundant data. Even if a sensor does not move, it still continues to capture scans that should be processed. This paper presents the novel filter that allows droping 2D scans that bring no new information to the system.

arxiv-2208-07114.title: Preventing Deterioration of Classification Accuracy in Predictive Coding Networks
arxiv-2208-07114.creator: Paul F Kinghorn, Beren Millidge, Christopher L Buckley
arxiv-2208-07114.description: Abstract Predictive Coding Networks (PCNs) aim to learn a generative model of the world. Given observations, this generative model can then be inverted to infer the causes of those observations. However, when training PCNs, a noticeable pathology is often observed where inference accuracy peaks and then declines with further training.

arxiv-2211-16998.title: Efficient classical algorithms for simulating symmetric quantum systems
arxiv-2211-16998.creator: Eric R. Anschuetz, Andreas Bauer, Bobak T. Kiani, Seth Lloyd
arxiv-2211-16998.description: Abstract In light of recently proposed quantum algorithms that incorporate symmetries in the hope of quantum advantage, we show that with symmetries that are restrictive enough, classical algorithms can efficiently emulate their quantum counterparts given certain classical descriptions of the input.

arxiv-2301-02948.title: Quantum synchronization effects induced by strong nonlinearities
arxiv-2301-02948.creator: Yuan Shen, Wai-Keong Mok, Changsuk Noh, Ai Qun Liu, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Weijun Fan, Andy Chia
arxiv-2301-02948.description: Abstract A paradigm for quantum synchronization is the quantum analog of the Stuart–Landau oscillator, which corresponds to a van der Pol oscillator in the limit of weak (i.e. vanishingly small) nonlinearity. Due to this limitation, the quantum Stuart–Landau oscillator fails to capture interesting nonlinearity-induced phenomena such as relaxation oscillations.

arxiv-2301-13779.title: FLAME: A Small Language Model for Spreadsheet Formulas
arxiv-2301-13779.creator: Harshit Joshi, Abishai Ebenezer, José Cambronero Sanchez, Sumit Gulwani, Aditya Kanade, Vu Le, Ivan Radiček, Gust Verbruggen
arxiv-2301-13779.description: Abstract Spreadsheets are a vital tool for end-user data management. Using large language models for formula authoring assistance in these environments can be difficult, as these models are expensive to train and challenging to deploy due to their size (up to billions of parameters).

arxiv-2310-10798.title: Poisson Count Time Series
arxiv-2310-10798.creator: Jiajie Kong, Robert Lund
arxiv-2310-10798.description: Abstract This paper reviews and compares popular methods, some old and some very recent, that produce time series having Poisson marginal distributions. The paper begins by narrating ways where time series with Poisson marginal distributions can be produced. Modeling nonstationary series with covariates motivates consideration of methods where the Poisson parameter depends on time.

arxiv-2406-02997.title: Residual Connections and Normalization Can Provably Prevent Oversmoothing in GNNs
arxiv-2406-02997.creator: Michael Scholkemper ∗, Xinyi Wu, Ali Jadbabaie, Michael T. Schaub, Department of Computer Science, RWTH Aachen University, schaub@cs.rwth-aachen.de
arxiv-2406-02997.description: Abstract Residual connections and normalization layers have become standard design choices for graph neural networks (GNNs), and were proposed as solutions to the mitigate the oversmoothing problem in GNNs. However, how exactly these methods help alleviate the oversmoothing problem from a theoretical perspective is not well understood.

arxiv-2406-10521.title: MALLM-GAN: Multi-Agent Large Language Model as Generative Adversarial Network for Synthesizing Tabular Data
arxiv-2406-10521.creator: Yaobin Ling, Xiaoqian Jiang, Yejin Kim
arxiv-2406-10521.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yaobin Ling, Xiaoqian Jiang, Yejin Kim. In the era of big data, access to abundant data is crucial to driving research forward. However, such data are often inaccessible due to privacy concerns or high costs, particularly in the healthcare domain. Generating synthetic (tabular) data can address this, but existing models typically require substantial amounts of data to train effectively, contradicting our objective of solving data scarcity.

arxiv-2406-15647.title: Generating Music with Structure Using Self-Similarity as Attention
arxiv-2406-15647.creator: Sophia Hager, Kathleen Hablutzel, and Katherine M. Kinnaird
arxiv-2406-15647.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sophia Hager, Kathleen Hablutzel, and Katherine M. Kinnaird. Despite the innovations in deep learning and generative AI, creating long term structure as well as the layers of repeated structure common in musical works remains an open challenge in music generation. We propose an attention layer that uses a novel approach applying user-supplied self-similarity matrices to previous time steps, and demonstrate it in our Similarity Incentivized Neural Generator (SING) system, a deep learning autonomous music generation system with two layers.

arxiv-2409-12555.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
arxiv-2409-12555.creator: Mollie S Jagoe Brown, Floor Schipper and Arthemy V Kiselev
arxiv-2409-12555.description: Abstract Kontsevich constructed a map from suitable cocycles in the graph complex to infinitesimal deformations of Poisson bi-vector fields. Under the deformations, the bi-vector fields remain Poisson. We ask, are these deformations trivial, meaning, do they amount to a change of coordinates along a vector field?

arxiv-2410-17024.title: A probe of the maximum energetics of fast radio bursts through a prolific repeating source
arxiv-2410-17024.creator: O. S. Ould-Boukattine, P. Chawla, J. W. T. Hessels, A. J. Cooper, M. P. Gawroński, W. Herrmann, D. M. Hewitt, J. Huang, D. Huppenkothen, F. Kirsten, D. C. Konijn, K. Nimmo, Z. Pleunis, W. Puchalska, M. P. Snelders
arxiv-2410-17024.description: Abstract Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are sufficiently energetic to be detectable from luminosity distances up to at least seven billion parsecs (redshift z > 1 z>1 ). Probing the maximum energies and luminosities of FRBs constrains their emission mechanism and cosmological population. Here we investigate the maximum energetics of a highly active repeater, FRB 20220912A, using 1,500 h of observations.

pmc-13210852.creator: Nanshin Nansak, Leo Creedon, Denis O’Mahoney, Ramen Ghosh, Marion McAfee
pmc-13210852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The microstructure of semicrystalline bioresorbable polymers is central to their biomedical performance because the crystalline content influences both the mechanical stability and the degradation behaviour. Experimental studies have shown that crystallinity evolves concurrently with mass loss during enzymatic degradation. However, most existing models represent the material as a single homogeneous structure, preventing them from capturing this microstructural evolution or the state-selective mechanisms that drive it.
